analysis:
The PR changes only documentation: docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (new 'prompt geometry' paragraph near lines 549-567) and docs/architecture/inference.md (scheduler table rows at ~1087-1090, new 'Prompt geometry' section at ~1101-1159, new invariants 8-9 at ~2041-2060). No executable code, wire protocol, attestation, key handling, authorization or encryption paths are modified, so no regression against the TB-002, TB-003, TB-009 or TB-011 controls or the A-001 through A-017 assets can be shown from the supplied evidence.

Security-relevant content documented: Gemma 4 now defaults to a 2048-token plain prefill chunk and 4096-token step budget, while bidirectional media blocks keep a 512-token chunk. The docs claim that the paged pool's maxPrefillChunk, KV grants, windowed-ring charges and load quotation are unchanged, and that the activation peak of 3.73 GiB stays inside the 5.5 GiB default reserve. The docs also say a block-bearing chunk can start at a block and extend over the whole block, with the step budget raised to at least 1,120 tokens. The related availability/memory-exhaustion concerns (T-016 and T-029 in spirit, and the memory-cap invariants) depend on the unseen code in EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift (prefillGeometry, usesWidePrefillChunk, gemma4MaximumMediaBlockTokens) and SchedulerV2.swift. I could not verify those implementations, so the claims remain unverified contracts and not findings.

The docs also describe DARKBLOOM_CBV2_* overrides that enter the complete-checkpoint numerics fingerprint (PrefixCachePolicy.completeCheckpointIdentity), which is relevant to T-041 prefix-cache identity. It is described as unchanged in kind. The accompanying code change, if any, should be checked to confirm that the Gemma 4 default geometry change enters that fingerprint so that cached KV is not reused across a differing numerics geometry. It should also be checked against the TTL and HMAC posture of T-041, which this docs-only PR does not alter. There is no new attack surface from the documentation itself.
